key_insight: FlatSounds reveals that current video-to-audio models can sound plausible yet fail to reflect underlying physical causes; targeted counterfactuals and single-video pattern tests expose these gaps in physical reasoning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of evaluation methods that test whether V2A models capture true physical relationships (causal/parameter changes) rather than only producing perceptually realistic audio.
method: Construct controlled counterfactual pairs where a single physical factor (e.g., material, impact force, distance) is changed while everything else is held constant to test sensitivity to that factor.
Design single-video pattern tests that probe whether models respond consistently to within-video parameter variations and recurring physical patterns.
Provide benchmark metrics and aggregated analyses that measure physical correctness (factor sensitivity, consistency) in addition to perceptual quality.
impact: FlatSounds enables rigorous auditing of V2A models for causal/physical fidelity, guiding development of models that generalize correctly to interventions — important for robotics, simulation, and multimodal reasoning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side counterfactual panels: two near-identical video frames with an annotated differing physical factor and their generated audio waveforms/spectrograms
Factor-sensitivity grid: heatmap showing model responsiveness to each single-factor intervention across models
Single-video timeline: annotated video with corresponding predicted audio events illustrating consistency or failure modes
Summary metrics dashboard: bar charts for physical-correctness scores vs perceptual-quality scores per model
paper_authors: Tingle Li, Siddharth Gururani, Kevin J. Shih, Gantavya Bhatt, Sang-gil Lee
